finding_status.notes: Empirically disproven, not just argued. Built a minimal reproduction of the exact pattern (chmod 555 on a directory in a builder stage, plain `COPY --from=builder --chown=...` with no `--chmod` in the next stage) through `gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.24.0-debug` via podman — the same tag as this project's pinned private-ECR Kaniko image (093899590031.dkr.ecr.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/kaniko-project/executor:v1.24.0-debug), since the private registry itself needs AWS auth this session doesn't have. Result, read directly from the output layer tarball: `venv/` came out `dr-xr-xr-x` (555) — the chmod bit survived the cross-stage COPY exactly. The Kaniko permission-loss bugs found during research (GoogleContainerTools/kaniko#647, #2240) were reported on v1.8.1/v1.9.0 and are fixed by v1.24.0. The Dockerfile:53-54 comment's assumption is correct for the pinned version. Also noted in the same conversation: a `RUN test ... = "555"` build-time assertion (the alternative fix the original review proposed) would itself trigger a full Kaniko filesystem snapshot on every RUN, i.e. the same cost the branch's revert commit (0efd67b5a) was specifically trying to avoid — so it wasn't a free mitigation even if CR-001 had held up.

Branch owner confirmed this branch merges to main via squash — individual commit subjects inside the feature branch (including the 4 missing an EPMCDME prefix) never land in master history; only the squash-merge commit message does, and that carries the ticket reference. git-workflow.md's commit-format gate is evaluated against what actually reaches main, so the per-commit violations inside this branch are moot.

Downgraded, not proven safe — the underlying uncertainty is unchanged, only the severity assessment. Confirmed pytest-xdist is a direct pyproject.toml dependency (`pytest-xdist = "^3.6.1"`), so the original finding's 'entire pytest invocation would error out' framing is not about the package being absent — it can only be triggered by an execution environment that blocks OS-level subprocess spawning (fork/exec), e.g. a restrictive seccomp profile, gVisor sandbox, or a container with pids_limit=1. No evidence was found (or exists in this repo) that the 'external CI job' referenced in commit c7424561d is such an environment; ordinary GitLab shared/docker/k8s executors allow subprocess spawning by default. Given the original finding already called this 'ambiguous... rather than a confirmed break,' treating it as blocking overstated the risk. Non-blocking until there's an actual report of it failing somewhere. If it ever does, the correct fallback is `PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-n 0"` (keeps the xdist plugin loaded so `-n 2` in addopts stays a recognized argument, just runs 0 workers) — not `PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-p no:xdist"`, which conflicts with the hardcoded `-n 2` in addopts and produces its own 'unrecognized arguments' failure.
